title: Maximal geometric branch locus and its one-step blowup
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover), let $B\subset X$ be a normal crossings divisor, and let $D\subset B$ be a nonempty reduced union of irreducible components. A normal crossings divisor means a reduced effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor) [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] which, etale locally [def-weil-etale-morphism], has equation $t_1\cdots t_r=0$ for distinct members of a regular system of parameters; a regular system of parameters in a regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is a set of $\dim R$ elements generating $\mathfrak m$. A geometric point is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed; in an etale chart through it, its geometric prime is the prime of the chart ring underlying its image. Define $b_D(\bar x)$ to be the number of coordinate factors for $D$ whose images lie in that geometric prime (equivalently, the number of local branches of $D$ through $\bar x$). These numbers have a finite maximum $m\geq1$. The locus where $b_D=m$, endowed with its reduced closed subscheme structure $M$, is a nonempty regular closed subscheme of $X$. Etale locally at each point of $M$ one can choose the above parameters so that $D=V(t_1\cdots t_m)$, $B=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ with $m\leq r$, and $M=V(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$. Let $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_M(X)\to X$ be the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] and $D^+$ the strict transform of $D$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Then $D^+$ is empty or a normal crossings divisor and $b_{D^+}(\bar y)\leq m-1$ at every geometric point of $X^+$.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8, printed p. 118; local computation in 4.2.8--4.2.9, printed pp. 120--121. Geometric branches are used to make the normalization-fibre count precise.

proof.text: Choose pointed affine etale normal-crossings neighborhoods on which $D$ is a product of a selected subset of the coordinate factors for $B$, and discard factors which are units at the chosen point by shrinking the neighborhood. The local branch-count lemma [lem-trf-nc-coordinate-max-stratum] identifies the geometric branch function on each neighborhood, makes it independent of the coordinates, and writes each locus $b_D\geq k$ as a finite union of closed coordinate intersections. Etale maps are flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Their open images cover the quasi-compact scheme $X$, so finitely many of these charts cover $X$ by their images. The finitely many numbers of factors bound every $b_D$, and nonempty $D$ supplies a positive value; thus a largest attained value $m\geq1$ exists. For any $k$, the complement of $\{b_D\geq k\}$ is the union of the open images of its open inverse images in these charts, so $\{b_D\geq k\}$ is closed. Consequently the nonempty locus $T=\{b_D=m\}$ is closed, and $b_D<m$ outside $T$.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8, printed p. 118: multiplicity stratification and deepest closed stratum.

proof.text: Give $T$ its reduced induced closed structure $M$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. At any geometric point of $T$, choose the chart in Step 1 centered at that point; its equation for $D$ has exactly $m$ nonunit factors. In that chart the inverse image of $T$ is $V(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$, regular and reduced by [lem-trf-nc-coordinate-max-stratum]. By the reduced-pullback assertion of [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent], the pullback of $M$ is exactly this reduced coordinate intersection; this proves equality as closed subschemes, not merely as sets. The map from this pullback to $M$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], hence induces flat local maps by [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism]. Both local rings are Noetherian, since $M$ is closed in locally Noetherian $X$ and its etale charts are locally Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] to deduce that the local ring of $M$ at the chosen point is regular. This proves regularity of $M$ and the asserted simultaneous local equations for $B$, $D$ and $M$.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.8, printed p. 118; reduced coordinate center and regularity descent (Stacks 00OF).

proof.text: Let $v:U\to X$ be one of the etale charts at a point of $M$. It is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so the comparison of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] and identifies the blowup along $M\times_XU$ with $U\times_XX^+$. We also identify strict transforms scheme-theoretically, as follows. Put $P=D\times_XX^+$, $S=D^+\subset P$, and $\Omega=D\setminus M$, viewed as the preserved open in $P$. By [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization], $S$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of $\Omega$. The open immersion $\Omega\to S$ is quasi-compact: the pulled-back finite-type center ideal has finitely many generators on any affine open, and its complement is the finite union of their principal opens. It is quasi-separated since it is an open immersion. Its scheme-theoretic image is $S$ by the closure definition [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure]. The projection $S\times_XU\to S$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Thus [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] makes $\Omega\times_XU$ scheme-theoretically dense in $S\times_XU$. The latter is closed in $P\times_XU$ by [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change]; it is exactly the closure of that open: any closed subscheme containing the open has zero defining ideal after restriction to $S\times_XU$, by density. This is the strict transform of $D\times_XU$ by the same closure characterization. The identification respects the inclusions into $U\times_XX^+$.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.8, printed p. 118 (etale localization); Stacks 0805 and 081I for the blowup and the preserved-open closure.

proof.text: Over $M$, Step 2 supplies pointed affine etale charts with $D_U=V(t_1\cdots t_m)$ and $M_U=V(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$. Apply [lem-trf-nc-coordinate-blowup-branch-drop] to these charts, using Step 3 to identify their blowups and strict transforms with the pullbacks from $X^+$. At each chosen point $y$ of the $i$-th blowup chart its equation is $\prod_{j\ne i}t_j'=0$; exactly the factors vanishing at $y$ are members of a regular system of parameters of the local ring there, and the remaining factors are units. This proves normal crossings pointwise and gives at most $m-1$ geometric branches. For $m=1$ the product is $1$, so the strict transform is empty on these charts. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], the charts give etale neighborhoods of every geometric point of $X^+$ lying over $M$, which is precisely the local criterion for the asserted normal-crossings condition and branch bound.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.8 and Lemma 4.2.9, printed pp. 118 and 121: the standard charts, interpreted at each local ring.

proof.text: Over $X\setminus M$, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies the blowup with $X\setminus M$, and [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement] identifies $D^+$ with $D$ there. Hence $D^+$ is normal crossings there and Step 1 gives $b_{D^+}=b_D<m$, or equivalently $b_{D^+}\leq m-1$. Together with Step 4 this covers every geometric point of $X^+$.
